title: Northern Ireland can win group if they avoid defeat in Hungarian capital
text:
Plan is to win the group insists NI manager Michael O’Neill

 Sport Plan is to win the group insists Michael O’Neill
 By Damian Mullan 
 Published 17th Nov 2026, 12:04 GMT Terry Devlin scored the only goal as Northern Ireland defeated Ukraine on Saturday evening. | IFA. Michael O’Neill says the objective for Northern Ireland when they face Hungary on Tuesday night is ‘to win the group.’
 The two nations are due to meet at the Puskas Arena in Budapest in a top of the table clash in League B Group 2 of the UEFA Nations League (19.45 GMT kick-off).
 Northern Ireland currently top B2 with 11 points from their five games to date, while the Hungarians have 10 points from five matches.
 It’s the final group game for both teams. O’Neill’s side only need a point to win the group and gain automatic promotion to League A for the sixth edition of the competition in 2028/29.
 The Northern Ireland manager told media at the pre-match press conference at the Puskas Arena that the aim is to win the group.
 The 0-0 draw between the two teams in Belfast back in September was a tight affair and O’Neill believes tomorrow night’s game will be something similar.
 He also said he wants his team to play with the same conviction, spirit, organisation and belief that they have shown in the five previous games in B2.
 He further said the most pleasing thing for him about the Nations League campaign to date, apart from keeping clean sheets in all five games, is the growth of the squad and how the players have learnt to adapt to some challenging circumstances.
 Trai Hume told the media the players are excited at having the chance to finish top of the group and will relish playing in front of a full house at the 67,000-capacity Puskas Arena. Around 2,700 Northern Ireland fans will be at the game.
 O’Neill, who received a touchline ban after picking up a second yellow card of the campaign in the match against Ukraine on Saturday, said his coaching staff have enough experience to cope with his absence from the dugout. He stressed that his tactical work will be done in advance.
 Striker Jamie Donley is suspended for the game, too. He also picked up his second yellow of the campaign against the Ukrainians. All the other players in the squad are fit and available for the final B2 encounter, according to the boss.
 Thanks to their performances so far Northern Ireland have already guaranteed a play-off for a place in League A next time around – and they will also be in Pot 2 for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw being staged in Belfast next month.
 But after the 1-0 victory against Ukraine both striker Josh Magennis and midfielder Shea Charles insisted the team will be going out to win against the B2 top seeds tomorrow night and qualify automatically for League A in the next edition of the Nations League.
 "We try and win every single game. If you don't, there's no point going," said Magennis, who will win a 95th cap if he plays in Budapest.
 And Shea Charles said: "I think we'll still try and go there and win. We know it's going to be a challenge. It'll be tough. We've got to go out there and play the way we've been playing."
 Former Brescia, Sampdoria, Eintracht Frankfurt and Piacenza defender Marco Rossi has been Hungary’s head coach since June 2018.
 His teams typically line up in a 4-2-3-1 formation with two defensive midfielders usually included in the starting XI to enable Liverpool midfielder and national team captain Dominik Szoboszlai freedom of movement in the opposition’s final third and the team’s full-backs to play in advanced positions.
 Whether operating with a back four or with a back five on occasions, Hungary’s full-backs will typically support their team’s attacking movements. One of those full-backs is Szoboszlai’s Liverpool teammate Milos Kerkez, who brings creativity to the team from the left full-back position.
 Another Hungarian midfielder with strong pedigree is Andras Schäfer, who plays in the Bundesliga with Union Berlin.
 In Belfast back in September Hungary were without high-scoring AEK Athens striker Barnabás Varga through injury. However, he returned to the fold in the game against Georgia on Saturday and scored the winner.
 Tuesday night's game is being shown live on BBC One Northern Ireland and BBC iPlayer from 19.15. You can also listen to commentary on BBC Sounds and BBC Radio Ulster and you can follow the game on Northern Ireland social channels.
